detail.longDescription:
Back home, I finally had the opportunity to test Qwen3.8, and wow, this thing is good!

Some tech publications, looking at you, Heise, claimed that Qwen3.8 "runs on any consumer GPU". That is a little misleading. There are consumer GPUs with enough VRAM, like the RX 7900 XTX with 24 GB, but that's already a fairly expensive GPU. And once you're getting into RTX 4090 territory and beyond, I wouldn't exactly call that typical consumer hardware anymore xD

But it turns out Qwen3.8 is actually quite usable on my RX 6700 XT (ROCm) with 12 GB of VRAM and 16 GB of system RAM (and 32 GB swap).

I first tried asking it in German: "Was ist Photorespiration?" The answer was actually pretty good, but German grammar learned from Yoda, Qwen has!

So I asked the same question in English instead: "What is photorespiration? Explain the biochemical pathway and why it occurs."

This time it produced a much cleaner and more detailed answer, 2620 tokens long, covering RuBisCO, the glycolate pathway, and the roles of chloroplasts, peroxisomes and mitochondria.

It simplifies a few things here and there, but overall the explanation is scientifically correct. For a local model, this level of detail is honestly awesome.

Generation speed: 7.79 tokens/s

For the test, I even dug out the Hyprland setup I made for AI about half a year ago and haven't used since. Apparently it finally has a reason to exist again xD

The screenshots show the actual GPU and system load with nvtop and htop while Qwen3.8 was running.
